questions: Which reported legacy numerical/news/corporate/policy counts and fields actually exist?
Which are aliases, derived fields, assumed/fabricated histories, or unrecovered source records?
Do available original artifacts establish dated non-holdout H1 or H2 information beyond the earlier strict as-of ledger?
prespecified_rules: Do not read or summarize reserved target outcome values; target files supply calendar keys and observation-presence flags only if necessary.
Quarantine formula-generated registrations and unsafe legacy joins never become empirical predictors.
A recorded timestamp is not sufficient; inspect its source/generation code and original release/version evidence.
Preserve raw input files and all previous snapshots.
No assumed one-month publication lag or annual/quarterly-to-monthly imputation.
National shared data and operator/city-specific data remain distinct.
Use exact source/version/period keys and exact Decimal numeric comparison; differing source definitions and vintages are not silently merged.
Report dated selected-event metadata as selected-event metadata, not representative monthly sentiment or zero-news months.
No models, stationarity tests or final-test evaluation.
planned_outputs: Executable audit and source input hashes
Legacy-versus-native variable and corpus eligibility dictionary
Source-supported exploration eligibility ledger where possible
